what_happened: Job 20261114-055838-0d3t (code job: audit the reading checks against records and relax those without evidence) failed in planning, before any code was written. The planner reached its fixed 600-second deadline without finishing a plan. The event lists no critic findings, no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered, and no partial plan or reason was kept.
cause: The planner has a fixed 600s wall-clock deadline. It keeps no partial plan, gives no progress signal and has no resume or retry path. Nothing sizes a request against that deadline before planning starts. This request is an open-ended audit: it has to check every reading check against records and judge which lack evidence. That is a large, unbounded survey and not one bounded change. A deadline stop discards all planning spend and records no reason. This is the fourth planner-deadline failure in one day.
other_causes: The request bundles an audit (survey every check) with a change (relax the unsupported ones), so planning must do both before any code.
No earlier planner timeout was carried into later attempts, so the same deadline and scope were hit again.
open_hypotheses: The planner may have spent its time reading many records and check definitions, but the fields do not show what it was doing at the deadline.
The deadline may be too short for any audit-style request; the fields cannot confirm this.
The planner may have been slowed by something other than scope, such as load or slow tools.
contradictions: The earlier cases share a code-change request shape. This one is an audit, so scope-driven timeout is plausible but not proven.
prevention: Make the planner deadline survivable. Have the planner save a partial plan and a progress note at intervals. On a deadline stop, hold the job as resumable with that note instead of failing it. Before planning, flag requests that need a survey of many records and split them into a measuring job and a changing job. Record the planner's last activity when time runs out. The gate counts show no disagreements for any gate, so no gate should be relaxed or removed.
proposed_request: Make planning survive its 600-second deadline. (1) When the planner reaches its deadline, keep the partial plan and a short progress note, and hold the job as resumable rather than failed. (2) Record what the planner was doing when time ran out. (3) Before planning, if a request asks for a survey of many records or checks followed by a change, split it into a survey job that writes its findings to a doc and a separate change job. Acceptance: a test with a planner that never finishes shows the job held with a kept partial plan and a stated reason, not failed with nothing; a test shows a survey-then-change request is split into two jobs; the changelog entry is added.
